answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a sable as the anchor of the cost. A juniper stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a meadow holds the rep...
